title: What The Cello Knows (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 100bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal music philosophy absurdist Bach
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The cello sits in the register between the violin and the bass
It occupies the middle of the orchestra's harmonic space
Which is the most important place to be and the most overlooked
The cello is the instrument that held the whole thing booked

[Pre-Chorus]
I once read that the cello is tuned to match the human male speaking voice
Which explains why I feel addressed every time it makes its choice

[Chorus]
What does the cello know that I don't know?
It knows the warmth between the highest and the lowest note below
What does the cello know in the middle register?
It knows that the most important things are never on the poster
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The Bach suites for unaccompanied cello are the cello's autobiography
Six suites, no other instruments, just the cello's topography
Of the entire range of human experience from grief to joy
And back — in six suites — no strings, no voice, no decoy

[Bridge]
I heard the first suite once on a ferry between islands in the dark
The cello came through someone's phone speaker in the park
Deck area and it was the size of a playing card in audio
But the Bach came through regardless and it was stereo
Inside my chest — because that's what the cello does

[Outro]
Cello knows… warmth between the registers… cello knows
That's my boy
